newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen higher at start.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to move higher at the open Friday, but trading will be cautious amid triple witching expirations and worry about a possible rise in interest rates.

"We have all but resolved that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "At this point, it will be a major surprise if the Fed does not tighten."
The Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meets next Tuesday.
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said the market would continue to focus on interest rates, with triple-witching adding volatility.
"There will be a lot of volatility as far as volume is concerned," he said. "I think we are heading for a higher opening, but then the market will continue to focus on rates.
"At this stage of the game the market is expecting an interest rate hike, and anything which suggests otherwise will cause nervousness because a 25-basis-point increase has already been discounted."
Thursday saw a very mixed market, with the Dow industrials led lower by a sell-off in Philip Morris Cos Inc while high technology issues bounced.
"The tech stocks showed some strength because they were oversold," said Wachtel. "When you take the Nasdaq down 10 percent in two months it will reach a point at which people will buy."
In Tokyo the Nikkei Average was up 139.45 points, or 0.75 percent, at 18,633.16.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was down 2.9 points at 4255.2.
Most U.S. shares staged a modest bounce in London, but trading was thin as many European investors stood on the sidelines ahead of the expiration of futures and options, dealers said.

Philip Morris, having lost 6-1/8 in New York yesterday, was quoted at 116-1/4 in London, up from its NYSE close at 115-7/8. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp bounced 1/4 to 41-7/8 after dropping 5/8 in New York.
High technology stocks were mixed in London. International Business Machines Corp was down 1/4 at 136-3/8. Intel Corp was up 1/4 at 133-1/2.
The dollar was weak in Hong Kong and edged higher in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly higher, with the long bond up 3/32 to yield 6.95 percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said technology stocks have been weak lately but investors have kept a "worshipful attitude" toward Intel and Microsoft Corp.

The New York Times's Market Place column said an indicator of relative valuations -- which measures the stocks in the Standard & Poor's 500-stock index against the stocks in the New York Stock Exchange composite index -- has reached extreme levels previously seen before the great bear market of 1973-74.
